findings.title: Having `view` permission on groups also passes `canManage()`.
findings.body: `canManage()` returns `hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)`. An admin who was given only the `view` scope on all groups therefore passes `canManage()` and `requireManage()`. That lets them do group-wide management, such as creating top-level groups through `GroupsResource`. This is privilege escalation from view to manage. Check only `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE` here, as `canManage(GroupModel)` already does.

findings.title: Group-ID filtering uses the authz resource's ID where it needs the group ID (the resource name).
findings.body: In V2 the group resource is named after the group ID (`resolveGroup` returns `group.getId()`), and the store generates the resource's own ID. This loop passes `groupResource.getId()` to `hasPermission`, which looks the resource up with `findByName`. That lookup misses, so the check falls back to the all-groups resource and the per-group `view-members`/`manage-members` permission is never evaluated. The loop then adds `groupResource.getId()` to the set, but callers put that set into `UserModel.GROUPS` and pass it to the user-count filters, which expect group IDs. As a result, user search and user counts filtered by group return wrong results. The all-groups type resource has the same type and can also end up in the set. Use `groupResource.getName()` for both the lookup and the returned ID, and skip the type resource. I could not check the `ResourceStore.create` signature to confirm how the ID is generated.
